nodes.label: Australia's intergenerational tax reform package
nodes.summary: From Treasurer Chalmers' March framing through the May budget package to lower-house passage in June — the most concrete intergenerational-equity fiscal reform in any OECD country in 2026.

nodes.label: EU Strategy on Intergenerational Fairness: institutional journey
nodes.summary: The first supranational intergenerational fairness framework moves from Commission adoption (March) through EESC hearings and GAC briefing to first-ever Council conclusions (May), drawing serious intellectual critique by June.

nodes.label: Loss and Damage Fund: first delivery cycle
nodes.summary: The Fund for responding to Loss and Damage moves from youth demands and a thin pledge base through a country-support window and a closed first BIM call, then defers first project approvals to December 2026 — the operational test of whether locked-in climate harm gets grants this…

nodes.label: UN Future Generations Envoy on hold; US names its own
nodes.summary: Pact paragraph 32(a) keeps the UN Special Envoy for Future Generations unfunded during UN80, while Washington appoints a national Special Envoy for Best Future Generations — multilateral stall against a branded national office.

nodes.label: ICJ climate advisory opinion: follow-through
nodes.summary: The downstream consequences of the July 2025 ICJ advisory opinion: UNGA endorsement (141-8) and the Right Livelihood Award for PISFCC, the youth movement that started it.

nodes.label: Lighthiser v. Trump youth climate litigation
nodes.summary: 22 youth plaintiffs challenge Trump fossil-fuel executive orders; Ninth Circuit oral arguments in April end in unanimous dismissal in June, deepening the US federal judicial barrier to youth climate claims.

nodes.label: New Zealand climate tort override vs Smith rights appeal
nodes.summary: Wellington legislates to bar emissions-damage torts after Smith v Fonterra, while the Supreme Court separately lists a three-day NZBORA/Treaty climate-rights appeal that the tort ban cannot extinguish.

nodes.label: US companion-bot child-safety statutes
nodes.summary: Oregon, Nebraska, and Connecticut enact companion or conversational-AI rules in one session: private right of action, bans on romantic role-play and variable rewards, and hourly minor disclosures — treating emotional AI as childhood infrastructure.

nodes.label: Votes at 16: consultation demand to UK bill
nodes.summary: EU Youth Dialogue respondents put votes at 16 at the centre of Youth Goal #1; the UK Representation of the People Bill then carries the first UK-wide franchise extension in nearly 60 years toward the 2029 election.

nodes.label: AI global governance architecture is institutionalising
nodes.summary: From Global Digital Compact Objective 5 and the UN AI scientific panel/dialogue track through EU AI Act implementation, national safety institutes, and Council of Europe rights instruments — AI governance is shifting from principles to permanent machinery, with youth and child-s…

nodes.label: Education equity & intergenerational mobility
nodes.summary: Discovered cluster around education, unesco — confirmed from 11 signals spanning 5 existing trend(s).

nodes.label: Future generations institutional machinery
nodes.summary: Dedicated institutions for representing future generations are multiplying: EU strategy and index, Welsh commissioner model, UNU platform, generational impact assessment laws, and SRM governance debates about the truly unborn.

nodes.label: Intergenerational equity goes mainstream
nodes.summary: Intergenerational equity language is migrating from advocacy into budgets, court citations, mass media and domains far beyond climate — disability policy, national security, space governance, fiscal federalism.

nodes.label: Intergenerational fiscal rebalancing
nodes.summary: OECD governments are redistributing fiscal burdens between generations through tax, pension, housing and benefit reform — Australia legislating, UK commissioning, Canada debating spending-side reform.

nodes.label: Youth climate & environment governance
nodes.summary: Structured pipelines from youth climate organizing into formal governance: national youth climate councils, COP31 talanoa dialogues, EU green policy dialogues, and long-term environment planning frameworks.

nodes.label: Youth climate litigation: international advance, domestic retreat
nodes.summary: International law is opening to youth climate claims (ICJ, UNGA, Bonaire) while US federal courts systematically close (Lighthiser, Genesis B., Wisconsin) — pushing strategy toward state courts and treaty mechanisms.

nodes.label: Youth digital protection regulatory wave
nodes.summary: One of the fastest-spreading regulatory trends in digital governance: under-16 social media bans across four countries in six months, G7 common principles, EU age verification — countered by OHCHR's safety-by-design framework.

nodes.label: Youth participation in governance institutions
nodes.summary: Youth voice is being institutionalized across multilateral and national governance — UN forums, EU dialogues, national youth councils — while exclusion persists (Zimbabwe, India) and youth political power erupts outside institutions (Nepal).

nodes.label: Chequebook COP
nodes.summary: A first finance package moves. The ICJ chain stays out of operative text, and youth standing does not travel with the money.

nodes.label: Double stall
nodes.summary: No operative ICJ language, no first FRLD package, and future-generations machinery stays on hold.

nodes.label: Operative duty
nodes.summary: COP31 cover decision carries the ICJ/UNGA chain, and the first FRLD package actually moves money.

nodes.label: Unfunded mandate
nodes.summary: Cover text and courts pick up the ICJ chain. The Loss and Damage Fund still cannot pay.
